To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the short‐terminal synaptic plasticity in the hippocampi is highly cell type dependent and that the short‐time plasticity in the CA1 region of hippocampus is different in the different cell type interneurons.
the short‐terminal plasticity of excitatiory postsynaptic currents in the hippocampi of mice is highly heterogeneous, and depends on the postsyaptic interneuron type.
the short‐ term plasticity of EPSPs in the CA1 region is cell type dependent and that the plasticity patterns are heterogeneous even within a given interneurone type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the short-term plasticity of excitatoy postsynaptic currents in the CA1 area of the mouse hippocampus.
the functional properties of the hippocampal circuitry, and provides a new approach to the study of hippocampal interconnections.
the functional properties of the short‐term synaptic plasticity of EPSPs and their dependence on the cell type of the postsynaptic interneurones in the CA1 area of the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the short‐terminal plasticity of EPSPs in hippocampal inter­neurones is cell type dependent and variable.
the short‐terminal plasticity is highly variable in all interneurone types, with no clear correlation to molecular markers or projection targets.
the short‐terminal plasticity of synaptic transmission is not a simple, stereotyped process, but rather a complicated, heterogeneous phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the short‐ term synaptic plasticity is cell type dependent with significant heterogeneity.
the short‐terminal synaptic plasticity in the CA1 region is highly variable, and the short‐term synaptic plasticity of a particular cell is not a simple reflection of the interneurone type.
the short‐ term plasticity of EPSPs depends on the interneurone type, and that the short‐ and long‐term plasticity are not correlated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasticity of individual synapses can vary greatly even within the same cell type.
the short‐ term plasticity of EPSPs is cell‐type dependent.
the short‐ term plasticity of EPSPs in CA1 interneurones is not only dependent on the presynaptic release probability, but also on the postsynaptically expressed receptors.
